title: An ESCAPE-policy name is injective but not decodable: across an array boundary it splits to a phantom empty segment
rationale: Under ESCAPE, join() escapes each segment against the separator and then joins across an array boundary with the arrayBoundarySeparator, which is emitted OUTSIDE the escaped alphabet. FlattenedPath.decodeSegments splits on every unescaped separator, so items__sku decodes to three segments with an empty one in the middle. NameCollisionPolicy.ESCAPE's javadoc used to claim the rendering was 'lossless and reversible'; that claim has been withdrawn, because reversibility is a property of an encode/decode PAIR and this package ships only the encode half. What ESCAPE does guarantee - injectivity, no two distinct source paths rendering alike - is now ENFORCED rather than assumed: checkCollision used to return before it checked anything under ESCAPE, and it no longer does. See enriched-escape-forged-array-boundary-is-refused. The divergence recorded here is what remains: a deliberate rendering convention that must not be parsed, with FlattenedField.arrayBoundaries() as the structural answer.
catchesBugClass: Any attempt to re-promise decodability. Escaping the boundary marker collapses items__sku to the single segment items__sku; escaping half of it yields items_\_sku, which is already the encoding of the genuinely different path [items, _sku], so the repair manufactures the collision it was meant to prevent. Both would move this recording. It also catches the harness being 'fixed': teaching FidelityEnriched.decodedPaths about arrayBoundarySeparator would flip this row LOSSLESS and delete the disclosure rather than earn it.
cannotCatch: It does not exhibit a two-paths-one-name COLLISION, only a wrong decode - under the default __ marker the forging segment would have to be the empty field name, which Avro forbids. The sibling enriched-escape-forged-array-boundary-is-refused is the row that reaches a real collision, by varying arrayBoundarySeparator, which no fixture did before it. This one also cannot detect the same hazard under FAIL, where nothing is escaped and the decode is wrong for a different reason.

predicted.detail: The declared path is [items, sku]; the decoded path carries an unnamed middle level. A consumer who took the old javadoc at its word and used the flattened name as a map key or JSON pointer reconstructs a three-level path. PREDICTION LEFT AS DEFECT ON PURPOSE: the measurement has not moved a byte and the phantom segment is still there; what changed is that the guarantee no longer claims otherwise, which is a deliberate reclassification recorded as a classificationOverride.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_METADATA vs DECODED_PATH, collisionPolicy ESCAPE
